title: Coloring digraphs with $Δ-b$ colors
summary: The dichromatic number of a digraph is the minimum number of colors needed to partition its vertex set into acyclic subdigraphs. A biclique is a set of vertices inducing all possible pairs of opposite arcs. For a digraph $D$, define $Δ(D) = \max_{v\in V(D)} \sqrt{d^+(v) \cdot d^-(v)}$. We prove that, for every fixed integer $b\in\mathbb{N}$, every digraph $D$ with $Δ(D) = Δ$ being sufficiently large with respect to $b$ either contains a biclique whose size exceeds $Δ-2b$ or has dichromatic number at most $Δ-b$.
